application.cv_markdown:
Henrik Andersson
Helsinki, Finland | h.andersson@mail.example | +358 00 000 0090

EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer
Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems, Espoo
2013 – present

Design and implementation of DSP algorithms for multi-channel receiver systems. Work has centred on time-domain and frequency-domain filtering for wideband receivers, testing and integration of FPGA-based processing chains, and development of internal tooling.

- Degree in physics (Merihaka University, 2012) directly applicable to the signal-theoretic foundations of the receiver work — Fourier analysis, spectral estimation, stochastic processes.
- Published two papers in ISRT Radar, Sonar & Navigation (2017, 2021) on adaptive interference cancellation techniques for multi-channel receivers, both as second author.
- All technical documentation written in English; English is the working language across the engineering division.
- Currently based in the Helsinki metropolitan area. Willing to relocate to Oulu for the right position.

PROJECTS

4-element beamforming demonstrator (personal project, 2022–2023)
Built a small 4-element UHF beamforming array as a side project, mostly to scratch an itch. Used four RTL-SDR dongles phase-locked to a common 28.8 MHz reference oscillator, fed through a custom PCB I designed in KiCad, with the beamforming algorithm running on a Raspberry Pi 4. The digital beamforming is a basic delay-and-sum implementation in C, with a small ncurses display showing the beam pattern in real time. It works — I can steer a null onto a local FM transmitter and pull a weaker signal out of the noise floor — but it has never been through any formal review, and the hardware is held together with SMA adaptors and electrical tape.

FPGA-based polyphase channeliser (C/C++, Tuulenkaari internal)
Wrote the C++ host-side control and data-routing layer for a polyphase channeliser implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale FPGA. The C++ code handles DMA buffer management, real-time streaming of channelised output to disk, and a diagnostic interface used by engineers during integration testing. Runs on a PetaLinux image on the FPGA's embedded ARM core.

Receiver test-automation framework (Python)
Developed and maintained an internal Python framework (pytest-based, ~12k lines) for automated regression testing of Tuulenkaari's receiver processing chains. The framework drives test-signal generators, captures output, and runs pass/fail checks against reference data. In continuous use since 2018; I am still the primary maintainer.

Signal-conditioning pipeline coordination (2019–2020)
Led a three-person sub-team responsible for re-architecting the signal conditioning stage of Tuulenkaari's primary receiver processing chain. Assigned module-level work, ran weekly integration meetings, and was responsible for the delivery schedule. Delivered on time; architecture has been stable since.

Kestrel 2020 involvement
Participated in the Kestrel 2020 "DIGIRECV" collaborative research project (2018–2021) on next-generation wideband receiver architectures. Project required verified EU work-authorisation status for all consortium members. I hold Swedish citizenship and permanent Finnish residency.

EDUCATION

MSc Physics — Merihaka University, 2012
Thesis: "Spectral estimation methods for wideband digital receivers"

SKILLS

RF test and measurement: vector network analyser calibration, spectrum analysis, power-meter measurements, antenna pattern characterisation
FPGA: Vivado, Xilinx SDK, VHDL (reading/modifying, not primary design)
OS: Linux (daily driver since ~2005), bash scripting
Version control: Git, SVN (legacy)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
After thirteen years at Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems I have a fairly clear picture of what I am good at and what I want to do next. My work has been almost entirely on wideband receiver processing chains — designing the algorithms, writing the FPGA host code, building the test infrastructure around it. It has been satisfying work and I am proud of the publications that came out of it. But the receiver processing side is mature in our product line now, and the projects coming through are incremental rather than new. I am looking for a role where the signal processing problems are harder and the engineering is closer to the physics.

Kaikuvaara's instrument work involves the kind of phased-array and beamforming problems I have been drawn to for a while — that is what prompted the hobby demonstrator I describe in my CV, trying to get my hands on the problem space in a way my day-to-day receiver work did not offer. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role reads like work I have been circling for years, and Oulu's focused engineering community is somewhere I could go deep on a problem rather than remaining a generalist.

My career at Tuulenkaari has been fairly linear — joined after finishing my physics MSc, grew into the senior role I hold now, built a team-lead track record along the way — but two things on my CV might look unusual. First, the beamforming demonstrator. It is a personal project with no institutional backing, and I realise that is an odd thing to include on an application for a senior engineering position. I put it in because it is the closest I have to hands-on phased-array work, and I wanted to be straightforward about what that experience is and what its limits are. It works, but it is four elements and electrical tape, not production hardware. Second, my embedded C/C++ and Python work both sit under "Projects" rather than the main job description. That is a presentational choice — they are core parts of my role at Tuulenkaari, but I found it clearer to describe them as discrete deliverables with their own scope.

What I would bring: deep familiarity with the full signal path from the RF front end to processed output, a decade of production C++ and Python in a real engineering team, and the discipline of someone who has maintained his own test frameworks long enough to know what "maintainable" actually means in practice. I have looked into what Kaikuvaara builds and I have a reasonable sense of where your technical challenges sit.

I am ready to relocate and can start with a standard notice period.

Henrik Andersson

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
